obligations.source_item: Corollary 2.10: any two functions satisfying the sorting specification for every input are pointwise equal and hence equal as functions.
obligations.correspondence: `UQ.sorters_eq_at` proves pointwise equality for arbitrary functions satisfying the ordinary pairwise/permutation contract at one input. `UQ.sorters_eq` uses the contracts for every input plus function extensionality. `UQ.sorters_eq_of_multiset` retains the printed multiset formulation. All quantify over arbitrary Type u and relation with Std.Antisymm; no totality, stability, decidable payload equality or default element is added.

obligations.source_item: Sorted-input best case, pp.21–22: for nonempty sorted xs, `runs xs=[xs]`, `Cmerge_all(runs xs)=0` and `Cnmsort xs=length xs-1`. Empty input has zero comparisons.
obligations.correspondence: `NR.runsOn_of_sorted` gives the single run for nonempty sorted input. NRC's three exact counts and runsRunBy_of_sorted give scan n−1. `NSC.mergeComparisons_of_sorted`, run_of_sorted, comparisons_of_sorted and comparisons_lower give zero merge work, exact best count and global lower bound; empty/singleton laws retain zero.

obligations.source_item: Repeated append versus cons/reverse, p.22: appending n singleton values to an initially empty ordinary-list accumulator has append-call subcost `n*(n+1)/2`; the full fixed-overhead builder therefore has quadratic worst-case time. Prepending those values and applying the verified accumulator reverse has linear work and the same ordered result.
obligations.correspondence: `LB.appendSubRun_empty_cost` gives n(n+1)/2; appendLoopRun_cost and appendBuildRun_cost expose loop/wrapper entries. `LB.consReverseBuildRun_value` and `LB.consReverseBuildRun_cost` give the same ordered result with 2n+3 work; `LB.realizations_agree`, `LB.appendBuildRun_quadratic_lower`, `LB.appendBuildRun_quadratic_upper` and `LB.consReverseBuildRun_linear_upper` provide the resource comparison. ELB checks order, duplicates, nonempty seeds and empty payloads.

obligations.source_item: Difference-list append, p.22: creating the composed builder has constant local work independent of the represented list lengths, and its value is function composition with the correct append order.
obligations.correspondence: `DL.createCompose_eq` gives constant capture work independently of both stored callbacks' application costs; `DL.compose_value` and `DL.compose_rep` give correct composition/append order. `EDL.expensive_capture` and ordered_composition separate creation from invocation.

obligations.source_item: Difference-list materialization, p.22: applying a finite builder built from identity, singleton-prefix and composition to a suffix has work bounded linearly in its construction representation, with exact value equal to its represented prefix appended to that suffix.
obligations.correspondence: `DL.Rep`, `DL.AppCost`, `DL.buildFrom` and `DL.build_appCost` give finite closure construction/application laws. `NRO.ascOpsBy_buildFrom` and runsOpsBy_buildAscending connect the actual source worker to the actual stored callback construction; buildAscending_rep, buildAscending_appCost, buildAscending_apply, buildAscending_counts_add_three and buildAscending_counts relate its construction/application measure to the emitted prefix, retaining arbitrary suffix values. Existing EDL padded/doubled examples separate output length, construction history and unfolded invocation occurrences.

obligations.source_item: The actual runs/asc/desc construction has `W_runs xs<=A*length xs+B` in the chosen closure/scanner model, with fixed constants, hence the single-run natural-sort execution has linear operational work as well as C02-108's linear comparisons.
obligations.correspondence: `NRO.runsOpsBy`, `NRO.ascOpsBy` and `NRO.descOpsBy` instrument the actual scanner, closure creation and invocation, descending conses, emitted outer-run construction and branch/entry work. runsOpsBy_work_le gives ≤6n+1; ascOpsBy_work_le requires AppCost f k and gives ≤k+6m+5; descOpsBy_work_le gives ≤6m+5 for an arbitrary existing accumulator. singleRunOpsBy binds the actual returned list to baseMergeOps on the explicit run-count≤1 domain, with value/spec and ≤6n+2. Nil/singleton executions are 2/4; ascending n≥2 is 6n−4, descending nonempty strict-chain execution is 3n+1.
